propositions: The parent-first cascade walk logic is duplicated across claim.py (lines 200-237) and transition.py (lines 421-493), with identical ghost/init preconditions, creating maintenance risk when the class of bugs (missing edges) recurs

The decision table _CASCADING_EDGES is accessed by both claim and transition surfaces, but claim cannot express edges other than open→in_progress, while transition knows all three edges: (open→in_progress):open, (closed→open):closed, (closed→in_progress):closed

The shared cascade module must extract only the walk (ancestor recursion, cycle guard, benign-race TOCTOU re-check, error rewrap), keep the decision table at transition.py:415, and inject resolve_parent and advance so each caller preserves its own write primitive

apply_inbound_events._cascade_inbound_status_parents must remain separate because its walk returns written event paths topmost-first, an ordering its suite pins that a recursive helper returning None cannot reproduce without complicating the signature
The reopen command already cascades via the (closed→open) edge and must continue to work after extraction
All three cascading edges must be exercised by parametrised tests driven from the live _CASCADING_EDGES table to prevent silent introduction of new edges
